item.title: Lunchbox Lecture Raleigh: NC's Capital of Baseball (Aug 19, 2026)
item.description:
From legendary players and memorable moments to the region's thriving minor league traditions, discover how baseball has shaped our communities—and why Raleigh continues to be a compelling contender for Major League Baseball.



David Gill is the Site Manager of Moore Square in downtown Raleigh. A Raleigh native, he holds a B.A. in History and Political Science from Appalachian State University and has spent much of his career in the museum and public history fields. A lifelong baseball fan, David enjoys exploring the stories, people, and history that have made the game an enduring part of North Carolina's culture.

item.title: Join Us for the Chavis–Dix Strollway Public Meeting on August 20 (Aug 18, 2026)
item.description:
Preserving history helps connect people with previous generations and provides lessons for the future. That’s where the Chavis-Dix Strollway comes in. The 1.3 mile Strollway will become Raleigh’s second cultural trail, featuring streetscape improvements, wayfinding signage, and interpretive elements that honor the community’s history. The city’s first cultural trail – the South Park Heritage Trail – is fully funded and currently in the design development phase.



Now partially funded, the Strollway is being advanced as a concept plan. Once complete, it will create a walkable, meaningful connection between two of Raleigh’s most cherished parks: Dorothea Dix Park and John Chavis Memorial Park. It will also expand the storytelling that celebrates our city’s rich cultural heritage.



As momentum builds, the Fourth Ward Association recently hosted a bus tour on Aug. 13 highlighting the history and heritage of Raleigh’s Third and Fourth Wards – stories that will be woven throughout the Strollway. The event drew an enthusiastic crowd and showcased the community’s excitement for what’s ahead.



If you’re interested in learning more, we invite you to join us for the next public meeting on Aug. 20 from 5:30 - 7:30 p.m. at the Greg Poole Jr. All Faiths Chapel (1030 Richardson Dr., Raleigh). We’ll begin with a project overview at 5:45 p.m., share the vision and scope of the Strollway, and present draft concepts and timelines. Most importantly, we want to hear your stories and experiences – your input will help shape the interpretive elements and wayfinding features along the trail. An online survey will be available after the meeting for additional feedback.



We hope to see you there! For more news and updates on Downtown Raleigh projects, please visit our website.

item.title: New Thornton Road Boat Launch - Now Open! (Aug 17, 2026)
item.description:
News Published 8/17/2026 Updated 8/17/2026



Developed in partnership with the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission , the Thornton Road Boat Launch features a concrete boat ramp, staging area, and a dedicated gravel parking lot (including space for trailers and an ADA-accessible parking space). 



To visit the Thornton Road Boat Launch, navigate to 6100 Thornton Road and proceed down the gravel driveway, off of the greenway parking lot, to reach the designated boat launch parking lot. 



The boat launch is available for free public use, between dawn and dusk. Only non-motorized watercraft (such as canoes and kayaks) may be launched. Note that paddlers must cross the Neuse River Greenway Trail to reach the boat launch – please be mindful of greenway users.  



To learn more about the Neuse River Blueway, river access, and river safety in Raleigh, visit https://raleighnc.gov/river-access.

item.title: Marsh Creek Camps Discover Their Love for Urban Agriculture (Jul 23, 2026)
item.description:
Marsh Creek Community Center



News Published 7/23/2026 Updated 7/24/2026



Summer X-Press, Teen X-Treme, and Camp Exploration dig in each week to track progress in the garden and participate in an activity that gives campers the opportunity to “grow” their interest in gardening. 



Led by Raleigh City Farm, campers have enjoyed participating in a wide range of activities, including upkeep, tracking plant growth, discussing sustainable farming practices, harvesting produce, and orchard care. Campers who find a passion for gardening join the weekly “Farm Club” for additional time on the farm.



While the Urban Farm is currently operational for education and volunteering, we anticipate the “pay what you can” farmstand will open for distribution in summer 2027. 



Contact Marsh Creek Community Center for more information on this unique partnership with Raleigh City Farm!

item.title: First Friday with Little Raleigh Radio (Aug 14, 2026)
item.description:
News Published 8/14/2026 Updated 8/14/2026



Join us for a live performance by the Veldt, interviews with the band, and listen to their 1998 record, Illuminated. Stop by the museum from 6 - 9 p.m. to get in on the action. The Veldt will play around 7:45 p.m.



Little Raleigh Radio is a fully independent community-powered internet radio station that amplifies creative audio entertainment and educational opportunities for the people of Raleigh, North Carolina. Groove History is a collaboration with the City of Raleigh Museum, exploring records that showcase Raleigh’s creative capital, rich roots, and artistic direction.



Raleigh’s the Veldt are pioneers of shogaze rock. Founded by twins Daniel Chavis (vocals, guitar) and Danny Chavis (guitar), The Veldt released four incredible albums in the 90s starting with the standouts Marigolds and Afrodisiac. However, their first record, Illuminated 1989, was mysteriously shelved amidst an internal A & R staffing shakeup at Capitol Records.



In November 2023, North Carolina’s 5BC records and Portland’s Little Cloud Records helped get the rights back to Illuminated 1989. Despite being 30 years old, the album still feels ahead of its time with vocals that are clear and full of emotion, complementing the glimmering wall of music rather than allowing it to be absorbed. 



The record is proving as foundational now as it would have in the late 80s, and Little Raleigh Radio's Groove History is pleased to showcase it at the City of Raleigh Museum's First Friday event.



Location: City of Raleigh Museum
Date: Friday, Sept. 4
Time: 6 - 9 p.m.
Cost: Free
Ages: All

item.title: Car Care Series (Jul 29, 2026)
item.description:
Jaycee Community Center



News Published 7/29/2026 Updated 7/29/2026




All Classes
Ages: 16 and up
Cost: $25 Residents / $40 Non-residents
Register on RecLink



Location: Jaycee Community Center
Date: Tuesday, Sept. 1
Time: 6 - 8 p.m.



Whether you are a brand-new driver or you just want to feel more prepared, this class will give you the practical skills and roadside confidence needed to give you greater peace of mind and tools to take better care of your car.



Location: Jaycee Community Center
Date: Tuesday, Sept. 15
Time: 6:30 - 8 p.m.



You will go from feeling deflated to elated when we explore the gripping world of tread, plugging, changing, tire types, tires pressures, and how to access more information about your tires specifically. So, slow your roll and stop on by!



Location: Jaycee Community Center
Date: Wednesday, Sept. 23
Time: 6:30 - 8 p.m.



Instead of “braking” your spirits and the bank, stop by today to learn about “braking” your car instead. In this class we will go over tips to help guide conversations with mechanics, as well as tips to replace and maintain your brakes.



Location: Jaycee Community Center
Date: Tuesday, Sept. 29
Time: 6:30 - 8 p.m.



Pop your hood and let's learn about the “secret juices” that keeps your car rolling. In this class we will learn about what and where certain fluids are located, why does my dashboard light up like a Christmas tree, and how to keep up with those “secret juices.”



Location: Jaycee Community Center
Date: Tuesday, Oct. 6
Time: 6:30 - 8 p.m.



Get ready to “spark” your curiosity and take “charge” of your car battery. In this class we will learn about the different types of batteries, how to find one for you, new vs old, and where it is located. We will also go over the electrical systems of the car and how they all work together. Warning: this class may cause surges of high confidence and excitement!
